svg.aria-label: Three-stage architecture. Stage 1 image preparation: an image is converted to grayscale and resized to 128 by 128, tiled into 256 non-overlapping 8 by 8 patches, each flattened and L2-normalised into a 64-amplitude state, and expanded into 32,640 patch pairs each carrying a displacement. Stage 2 quantum comparison: the 15-wire swap-test circuit scores one pair per evaluation. Stage 3 mask formation: scores are thresholded, both patches of every matched pair are painted into the mask, connected components give boxes, and the matched-pair count gives the verdict.

g.text: Stage 1 : Image Preparation — every operation performed on pixels
every pixel in exactly one patch
free invariance to CoMoFoD's BC category
pair every patch with every other
“does region A reappear at region B?”
ψ₀, ψ₁ ∈ ℝ⁶⁴ + Δ → one circuit input
this pairing IS the copy-move question;
cost is O(N²) in patch count
Pure Swap-Test Siamese QNN — one circuit evaluation compares ONE patch pair (15 wires, 32 ms)
PQC ×3 — angle = θ + pixel·π (re-uploading) + CNOT ring
shared θ (Siamese) — 54 angles, ONE tensor drives both registers
CSWAP ×6 — ancilla-controlled swap of the WHOLE register, one gate per qubit pair
CRY ×2 — offset modulates the interference fringe
identical patches → swapping changes nothing → perfect interference → ⟨Z⟩ = 1 · orthogonal patches → no interference → ⟨Z⟩ = 0
⟨Z⟩ = |⟨ψ₀|ψ₁⟩|² — the squared overlap of the two patch states = their similarity
Stage 3 : Mask Formation — turning 32,640 scores back into an image
the only decision made from the
the pasted copy — never just one
display only — runs after the verdict
and feeds nothing back into it
No classical feature extractor, block matcher, offset vote
or morphology appears anywhere in stages 1–3.
Only trainable parameters: 58 circuit rotation angles.
